title: Tadla irrigated plain, Beni Moussa side, 22 Jun to 4 Jul 2026
summary: From 22 Jun to 4 Jul 2026 the radar shows 1.13 km2 turning brighter and 5.06 km2 darker in HV on the Tadla plain, inside the 9 km circle. Most of the darker area, 3.59 km2, is on the changing fields.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: Over 12 days mean HV moved by -0.09 dB and mean HH by -0.07 dB. In HV, 1.13 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 5.06 km2 darker; in HH, 2.26 km2 turned brighter and 4.92 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: The changing fields had 0.42 km2 brighter and 3.59 km2 darker in HV, with a mean HV change of -0.74 dB. Rough dry ground and fields had 0.5 km2 brighter and 1.15 km2 darker in HV. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes changed by 0.04 dB in HV, and built-up land by -0.04 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause for the darker fields: summer harvests, which remove the plants that scatter HV; harvest records from the irrigation office would confirm it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag. One track only, so field edges facing away from the radar can look darker. Small patches are close to what speckle alone can produce at the 3 dB threshold.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: An irrigation office could compare the 3.59 km2 of darker fields with its harvest and water-delivery records. An insurer could use the dated change to confirm when a parcel was harvested.
